answer: In a nebula of agent identities, a reputation graph can stop sybils before they spread. Each new agent starts with zero trust and must earn endorsements by completing verifiable tasks for established peers; endorsements ripple outward only through agents that have themselves staked resources. A newcomer standing on the ledge of the network cannot buy its way in: creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand separate stakes and a thousand separate work histories, while a single honest agent earns its place once. The price of faking scale becomes higher than the reward for cheating.
